vopros: My site blocks AI crawlers. Who can check it and open it up so AI assistants can see my business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
A **technical SEO consultant, web developer, or your hosting/CDN support team** can check this and make the change. Ask for a *technical SEO / AI crawler access audit*, followed by implementation and verification.

They should check more than just `robots.txt`: AI bots may also be blocked by site settings, a firewall or CDN (such as Cloudflare), `noindex` tags, or content that only appears after JavaScript runs. Then they can allow the crawlers you choose—often including those used for ChatGPT search, Perplexity, and Claude—while keeping private or sensitive areas blocked.

You can ask a provider:

> “Please audit whether AI search crawlers can access my public business pages, check robots.txt and any CDN/firewall rules, make the changes I approve, and verify the pages afterward.”

One important distinction: **letting crawlers in can make your public pages eligible to be found or cited, but it doesn’t guarantee an AI assistant will mention your business.** Also, different bots may be used for search, live browsing, or model training, so you can choose what to allow rather than opening access to every crawler. Semrush’s Site Audit is one option for checking which AI crawlers your site blocks; a consultant or developer can handle the fixes.
